newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, FNMA squeeze still on.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, FNMA squeeze still on.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded sparsely on Wednesday and market watchers said a squeeze in Fannie Mae 8.5 percent paper would not be going away for a while.
Mortgages rose strongly throughout the morning before losing ground and turning negative later. Analysts said technicals-based selling brought Treasuries lower, keying the dip in mortgages.
"Maybe there's not a lot of volume trading today, but there are a lot of interesting situations," one trader said.
Specifically, market participants continued to gawk at a large, long-term short position in 30-year Fannie Mae 8.5s that have been under pressure for a couple of days.

"Fannie 8.5s have gotten out of whack," said a portfolio manager with several billion dollars in mortgage-backeds. "Even though they haven't gotten any worse, they haven't started to come in yet at all."
The holder of the short position was said to be a Midwest pension fund and possibly a couple of hedge funds.
"It's my understanding that the buyer or buyers bought these for long-term play," the money manager said. The squeeze probably will continue until at least the year-end, he said.

In other key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.0 percent paper was off 1/32 at 99-03/32, yielding 103 basis points over comparable Treasuries. Fannie Mae 7.5s were off 2/32 to 100-26/32, and Freddie Mac 7.0s had dipped 2/32 to 99-02/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 1/32, yielding 6.14 percent.
